UK licensed product information contra-indicates the use of alfentanil in labour, or before clamping of the cord during caesarean section, because placental transfer means there is a risk of neonatal respiratory depression. Interactions For interactions associated with opioid analgesics, see p.103. Drugs that depress the heart or increase vagal tone, such as beta blockers and anaesthetic drugs, may pre- dispose patients given alfentanil to develop bradycar- dia and hypotension. Use of alfentanil with non-vago- lytic neuromuscular blockers may produce bradycardia and possibly asystole. The metabolism of alfentanil via the cytochrome P450 isoenzyme CYP3A4 may be reduced by potent inhibi- tors of this isoenzyme, resulting in a risk of prolonged or delayed respiratory depression. Reduced doses of al- fentanil may be required if given with a CYP3A4 in- hibitor such as cimetidine, diltiazem, erythromycin, fluconazole, itraconazole, ketoconazole, or ritonavir. Antibacterials.
